Triggers.value: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly

Threat.value: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.
When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.

issues.item: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: 'Risky Behavior' is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The other selected items describe fear-based reactivity, hypervigilance, sexual trauma triggers, and intrusive/reliving memory phenomena after rape. In that context, prominent risk-taking pulls in the opposite direction of the otherwise avoidance/vigilance-focused presentation and is not supported by appraisals or maladaptive-strategy items. This creates a within-node and cross-node coherence problem.

vignette: Nalini had always found solace in the rhythms of agricultural work. As a farmhand on a small family-owned plot in rural California, she spent her days tending to crops and livestock under the open sky. But it was this very setting that now seemed to hold a perpetual threat. The sound of dogs barking from neighboring farms made her flinch, transporting her back to the night when two men, accompanied by snarling animals, broke into her home and brutally assaulted her. The memory of that event had become a constant, uninvited companion. It would ambush her without warning - triggered by the rustle of leaves or the creaking of wooden beams in the farmhouse. When it did, Nalini was no longer in the present; she was reliving every detail, from the feeling of dirt beneath her fingernails to the taste of fear in her mouth. Her memories were a film that played over and over, each frame etched into her mind like acid on metal. Nalini had come to believe that her body knew more about danger than her mind did. Long before she could process what was happening, her heart would begin racing, her muscles tensing as if preparing for flight. At night, this hyper-vigilance made sleep an elusive luxury; she needed to stay alert, listening for any sign of intrusion, no matter how small. Intimacy with her husband had become a minefield of anxiety and avoidance. Nalini loved him dearly, but the mere thought of sexual situations now filled her with dread. She couldn't explain it - all she knew was that every time they tried to be close, images from that terrible night would intrude, leaving her feeling dirty and ashamed. It wasn't just memories or triggers; even physical touch had become a source of alarm. When someone touched her unexpectedly, Nalini's reaction was immediate and visceral - a jolt of adrenaline coursing through her veins like liquid fire. She had grown increasingly withdrawn, fearing the unpredictable nature of her reactions would drive away those she loved. As weeks turned into months, Nalini began to notice changes in herself that went beyond mere symptoms. Her relationships were suffering; her marriage was strained from lack of intimacy, and her relationships with friends and family were dwindling due to her inability to attend social gatherings or even answer the phone without anxiety. At work, she found herself taking longer routes through the fields, avoiding areas where dogs might be present. It wasn't until Nalini realized she couldn't keep living this way that she finally reached out for help. The thought of facing her memories head-on terrified her, but it was a terror she knew she had to confront. What frightened her most was losing herself completely - becoming trapped forever in the nightmare of that one awful night. As she sat in the therapist's office, Nalini's hands trembled slightly as she recounted her story. She was uncertain what lay ahead, but for the first time in years, there was a glimmer of hope - the possibility that with help, she might learn to tame the demons that haunted her and find peace once more in the simple rhythms of her daily life.
